pages.page_level_design_instruction:
## Home Page — Full Visual Design Direction

### Page Role & Emotional Arc
This is Rollout's front door: a warm, high-energy landing page that must make a visitor feel the joy of game night within two seconds of arriving. The page moves from excitement (hero) → credibility (stats) → understanding (features) → trust (testimonials) → action (CTA close). Each section has a distinct skeleton so the page never feels templated.

### Signature Moment — "Oversized Playmat Number Marquee" in the Stats Section
The page's single most memorable visual move lives in Section 2 (stats). The four stat values — "500+", "12,000+", "4.9 ★", "7 Days" — are rendered at a display scale of 96–120px in Fredoka One (the brand's accent font) in Rollout Blueberry (#3B6FE8), arranged in a horizontal scrolling marquee strip that bleeds edge-to-edge at full viewport width. The numbers are so large they are partially clipped by the container edges, functioning as type-as-image. This is calibrated perfectly to the Friendly Consumer App aesthetic: oversized, rounded letterforms, bright brand color dominating a full-bleed panel, joyful and readable at a glance. It is not a grid of cards — it is a kinetic typographic moment that makes the stats feel alive. The strip sits on a Cloud Chalk (#EDF0F7) background so the Blueberry numbers pop without harshness.

### Section Sequence & Skeleton Variation
1. **Hero** — Asymmetric split with illustration dominating the right 55%, text left-anchored, full-bleed Velvet Plum panel behind the headline with a Playmat Mint geometric cutout shape bleeding off the bottom edge.
2. **Stats** — Full-bleed edge-to-edge marquee strip (signature moment). No card grid. Numbers as display type.
3. **Feature Grid** — Alternating two-column asymmetric layout (not a uniform 4-column card row). Two features left-heavy, two right-heavy, each row offset vertically. Cloud Chalk background.
4. **Testimonials** — Horizontal scroll of three cards with Dice Coral left-border accents, on a Velvet Plum dark panel — the only dark section on the page, creating a strong density contrast after the airy features section.
5. **CTA Close** — Centered, sparse, Sun Token Yellow full-bleed panel with a large rounded die icon floating above the headline. Warm and conclusive.

### Color & Surface Rhythm
- Section 1 (Hero): Velvet Plum (#2D2250) background panel anchoring the left text column; Game Night White (#F7F9FC) for the right illustration zone.
- Section 2 (Stats): Cloud Chalk (#EDF0F7) full-bleed strip with Rollout Blueberry (#3B6FE8) oversized numerals.
- Section 3 (Features): Game Night White (#F7F9FC) background, Playmat Mint (#3ECFB2) illustrated icon fills, Velvet Plum headings.
- Section 4 (Testimonials): Velvet Plum (#2D2250) full-bleed dark panel — the page's lone dark section, creating visual drama and contrast.
- Section 5 (CTA): Sun Token Yellow (#FFD23F) full-bleed panel — warm, cheerful, conclusive.

The accent colors rotate expressively: Blueberry leads on interactive elements and the stats moment; Mint on feature icons; Coral on testimonial card borders; Yellow on the final CTA surface. No section reuses the same background as the one immediately before or after it.

### Typographic Hierarchy
- H1 (Hero): Nunito 800, 60–64px, Game Night White, sentence case, tight tracking.
- H2 (Section headings): Nunito 700, 38–42px, Velvet Plum on light sections / Game Night White on dark sections.
- Eyebrows: Fredoka One, 12px, wide letter-spacing 0.10em, in Playmat Mint or Dice Coral depending on surface.
- Stats display: Fredoka One, 96–120px, Rollout Blueberry.
- Body: DM Sans 400, 17px, 1.65 line-height, Felt Gray (#6B7A99) on light; Game Night White at 80% opacity on dark.
- CTA labels: DM Sans 500, 16px.

### Density / Whitespace Logic
- Hero: generous vertical padding (120px top, 100px bottom), illustration fills the right column to the edge — tight on the right, breathable on the left.
- Stats: compact vertical strip (80px padding), the oversized numbers are the padding — they fill the space.
- Features: spacious rows (100px vertical padding each row), deliberate whitespace between offset columns.
- Testimonials: medium density, cards have internal padding, the dark panel compresses perceived whitespace making it feel cozy.
- CTA: very sparse (140px padding top/bottom), centered, icon above text, two buttons side by side.

### Responsive Behavior
- Mobile: Hero stacks vertically — illustration moves above the text block, full-width. Stats marquee auto-scrolls on mobile; numbers remain at 72px. Feature grid becomes single column, each feature full-width. Testimonial cards become a swipeable carousel. CTA section stacks buttons vertically.
- Tablet: Hero maintains split but shifts to 50/50. Features collapse to 2×2 grid of equal columns.

### Fit Within Shared Design System
All fonts (Nunito, DM Sans, Fredoka One), all color tokens, rounded card corners (16–20px radius), illustrated icon style, and friendly CTA button shapes (fully rounded pill buttons for primary, outlined pill for secondary) are consistent with the shared design system. The home page is the most expressive page in the site — it sets the tone that subsequent pages inherit at lower amplitude.

section_design_plans.nl_prompt:
HERO SECTION — Asymmetric split layout, full viewport height (min 100vh), no top padding above the navigation bar. The section is divided into two unequal columns: left column spans 45% width, right column spans 55% width.

LEFT COLUMN — BACKGROUND & TEXT: The left column sits on a Velvet Plum (#2D2250) background that extends from the very top of the viewport to the bottom of the section, bleeding to the left viewport edge. At the bottom-left corner of this panel, a Playmat Mint (#3ECFB2) organic rounded shape (like a soft blob or rounded rectangle rotated ~15 degrees) bleeds partially off the bottom edge — approximately 120px tall, 200px wide — acting as a decorative anchor that connects the dark panel to the rest of the page. This shape should feel like a game piece or playmat corner, not a generic decorative blob.

Left column content is left-aligned, vertically centered within the panel, with 80px left padding and 60px right padding. Stack order top to bottom:
1. Eyebrow label: 'Welcome to Rollout' — Fredoka One, 12px, letter-spacing 0.10em, Playmat Mint (#3ECFB2), uppercase.
2. Headline: 'Your Next Favourite Game Night Is Waiting.' — Nunito 800, 60px, Game Night White (#F7F9FC), sentence case, line-height 1.1, tight tracking (-0.02em). Maximum width 480px. Allow the headline to break naturally across 3 lines.
3. Subheadline: '500+ games. Bottomless drinks. Zero bad times. Pull up a chair and play.' — DM Sans 400, 18px, Game Night White at 75% opacity, line-height 1.6, max-width 400px, 20px top margin from headline.
4. CTA button row: 40px top margin. Primary button: 'Book a Table' — pill shape (border-radius 999px), Rollout Blueberry (#3B6FE8) fill, Game Night White label, DM Sans 500 16px, 20px vertical / 36px horizontal padding. Secondary button: 'Explore the Game Library' — pill outline, 2px Game Night White border, Game Night White label, same sizing, 16px left margin from primary. Buttons sit in a flex row, left-aligned.

RIGHT COLUMN — ILLUSTRATION: The right column fills its 55% with the top-down café table illustration (home-section-1-asset-1). The illustration is positioned to bleed to the right viewport edge and to the top and bottom edges of the section — it is NOT contained in a card or rounded box. It fills the column like a full-bleed photograph. The illustration should feel as though the viewer is hovering above an active game table: colorful board game pieces, dice, cards, and drinks scattered joyfully. The illustration's background color should be Game Night White (#F7F9FC) or a warm near-white so it reads as a bright, airy space against the dark left panel. No drop shadow or border between the two columns — the hard vertical edge between Velvet Plum and the illustration background IS the divider.

The overall effect is a bold asymmetric split: dark, text-rich left panel anchored by the Mint shape at the bottom; bright, illustrated right panel that feels like a window into the café. This is not the standard SaaS 50/50 split — the 45/55 proportion and the full-bleed illustration treatment make it feel editorial and alive.

RESPONSIVE: On mobile, illustration moves to the top (full-width, 280px tall, cropped to center), then the Velvet Plum panel below it contains the eyebrow, headline, subheadline, and stacked CTA buttons (full-width primary, full-width secondary below). The Mint blob shape moves to the bottom-right corner of the Plum panel on mobile.

STATS SECTION — SIGNATURE MOMENT. This section is the page's most distinctive visual move. It is NOT a four-column card grid. It is a full-bleed horizontal display strip on a Cloud Chalk (#EDF0F7) background, 200px tall on desktop (240px on tablet), with 60px vertical padding top and bottom.

LAYOUT STRUCTURE: The section has two layers stacked vertically:

Layer 1 — Section header: Centered, 48px bottom margin below it. Eyebrow: 'By the Numbers' — Fredoka One, 12px, Dice Coral (#FF6B5B), letter-spacing 0.10em, uppercase. Headline below eyebrow (16px gap): 'A Whole Lot of Game Night Magic.' — Nunito 700, 38px, Velvet Plum (#2D2250), centered.

Layer 2 — The marquee strip: A full-viewport-width horizontal strip (no side padding, bleeds to both edges) that contains the four stat items laid out in a single horizontal row with generous spacing between them (use ~80px gap between items). Each stat item is composed of:
- Stat value (e.g., '500+', '12,000+', '4.9 ★', '7 Days'): Fredoka One, 96px on desktop / 72px on tablet, Rollout Blueberry (#3B6FE8), line-height 1.0. The '★' in '4.9 ★' is rendered in Sun Token Yellow (#FFD23F) at the same size.
- Stat description below the value: DM Sans 400, 15px, Felt Gray (#6B7A99), max-width 180px, centered under its value, line-height 1.5.

The four items are arranged so that the outermost items (500+ and 7 Days) are partially clipped by the viewport edges on desktop — the left edge of '500+' and the right edge of '7 Days' bleed beyond the viewport boundary. This intentional clipping makes the numbers feel monumental and kinetic, as if the data is too large to contain. On scroll, a subtle CSS marquee animation (slow, looping, left-to-right) can be applied — but the static layout already communicates the effect.

A thin 1px Playmat Mint (#3ECFB2) horizontal rule runs the full viewport width immediately above the marquee strip, and another runs immediately below it, serving as clean structural dividers.

RESPONSIVE: On mobile, the marquee strip becomes a 2×2 grid of stat items (no clipping), each item centered, with 40px vertical gap between rows. Numbers at 64px. The clipping effect is abandoned on mobile in favor of legibility.

FEATURE GRID SECTION — This section uses an alternating asymmetric two-column layout, NOT a uniform four-column card row. Background: Game Night White (#F7F9FC). Total vertical padding: 100px top and bottom.

SECTION HEADER (centered, max-width 640px, margin 0 auto, 72px bottom margin):
- Eyebrow: 'Why Rollout' — Fredoka One, 12px, Playmat Mint (#3ECFB2), letter-spacing 0.10em, uppercase.
- Headline: 'More Than a Café. It's a Game Changer.' — Nunito 800, 40px, Velvet Plum (#2D2250), centered, sentence case.
- Subheadline: 'We've designed every corner of Rollout to make your game night effortless and unforgettable.' — DM Sans 400, 17px, Felt Gray (#6B7A99), centered, max-width 520px, 16px top margin.

FEATURE ROWS — Two rows, each a 12-column grid split asymmetrically:

ROW 1 (Features 1 & 2): Left feature card spans 7 columns, right feature card spans 5 columns. The left card is taller and more prominent.
ROW 2 (Features 3 & 4): Left feature card spans 5 columns, right feature card spans 7 columns. The proportions SWAP to create visual rhythm and avoid symmetry.

Each feature card is a rounded rectangle (border-radius 20px), Cloud Chalk (#EDF0F7) fill, 40px internal padding. Rows have 32px vertical gap between them and 24px horizontal gap between cards within a row.

Each card contains:
1. Illustrated icon: 48×48px rounded square icon in Playmat Mint (#3ECFB2) fill (icon itself is white line art). Positioned top-left of the card.
2. Feature title: Nunito 700, 22px, Velvet Plum (#2D2250), 16px top margin from icon.
3. Feature description: DM Sans 400, 16px, Felt Gray (#6B7A99), line-height 1.65, 10px top margin from title.

Icon subjects (in order): 1) A stack of board game boxes for 'Massive Game Library'; 2) A speech bubble with a star for 'Expert Game Guides'; 3) A coffee cup with steam for 'Café & Bar Menu'; 4) A door with a game controller handle for 'Private Event Rooms'.

The asymmetric column swapping between rows means the page eye-path zigzags rather than scanning in a uniform grid — this creates the editorial energy appropriate to a Friendly Consumer App aesthetic that avoids the template feel.

CTA below the grid (48px top margin): 'See All Games' — pill button, Rollout Blueberry (#3B6FE8) fill, Game Night White label, DM Sans 500 16px, centered on the page.

RESPONSIVE: On tablet, both rows become 50/50 splits. On mobile, all four cards stack in a single column, full-width, 20px vertical gap.

TESTIMONIALS SECTION — This is the page's only full-bleed dark section, creating a dramatic density contrast after the airy feature grid. Background: Velvet Plum (#2D2250), full viewport width, 100px top and bottom padding.

SECTION HEADER (left-aligned, max-width content column, 56px bottom margin):
- Eyebrow: 'Guest Stories' — Fredoka One, 12px, Dice Coral (#FF6B5B), letter-spacing 0.10em, uppercase.
- Headline: 'Don't Just Take Our Word for It.' — Nunito 700, 40px, Game Night White (#F7F9FC), sentence case, left-aligned. Max-width 480px.

The header is intentionally left-aligned (not centered) to create asymmetric tension against the card row below, which is centered. This left-anchoring gives the section an editorial masthead quality.

TESTIMONIAL CARDS — Three cards in a horizontal row with 24px gap between them. Each card:
- Background: #1E1740 (a slightly darker shade of Velvet Plum, approximately 10% darker, giving depth within the dark panel).
- Border-radius: 20px.
- Left border: 4px solid Dice Coral (#FF6B5B) — this is the card's defining accent, the coral stripe that makes the card feel warm and energetic even on a dark surface.
- Internal padding: 36px.
- Width: equal thirds of the content column (~360px each at 1200px viewport).

Card content stack:
1. Star rating: Five ★ characters, Sun Token Yellow (#FFD23F), 16px, DM Sans, displayed as '★★★★★'. Top of card.
2. Quote body: The testimonial text — DM Sans 400, 17px, Game Night White (#F7F9FC) at 90% opacity, line-height 1.7, italic style, 16px top margin. The opening quotation mark is rendered in Fredoka One at 48px, Dice Coral (#FF6B5B), positioned as a decorative drop cap that sits above the first line of text and slightly overlaps it (negative margin-top on the text), giving the card a magazine pull-quote feel.
3. Attribution: Guest name/label — DM Sans 500, 14px, Playmat Mint (#3ECFB2), 20px top margin from quote. E.g., 'Priya M. — Regular Guest'.

CTA below cards (40px top margin): 'Join the Community' — pill outline button, 2px Game Night White border, Game Night White label, DM Sans 500 16px, centered. On hover, fill becomes Dice Coral with white label.

The dark Velvet Plum panel with Coral-bordered cards and Sun Token Yellow stars creates the coziest, most intimate section on the page — it feels like the inside of the café at night, warm and social.

RESPONSIVE: On mobile, cards stack vertically, each full-width. The section header becomes centered on mobile.

CLOSING CTA SECTION — This section is the page's warm, conclusive farewell. Background: Sun Token Yellow (#FFD23F), full-bleed, 140px top and bottom padding. The Yellow panel is a deliberate tonal surprise after the dark Velvet Plum testimonials section — it reads as a burst of sunlight and energy.

LAYOUT: Fully centered, single column, max-width 640px, margin 0 auto.

CONTENT STACK (all centered):

1. Die icon (home-section-5-asset-1): A bold six-sided die illustration with rounded corners, app-style flat aesthetic, in Rollout Blueberry (#3B6FE8) with white pip dots. Size: 72×72px. Positioned centered above the eyebrow, 0px bottom margin to eyebrow — it floats directly above the text stack as a playful punctuation mark. The icon is slightly oversized relative to the text below it, making it feel like a game token dropped onto the page.

2. Eyebrow: 'Ready to Play?' — Fredoka One, 13px, Velvet Plum (#2D2250), letter-spacing 0.10em, uppercase. 12px top margin from icon.

3. Headline: 'Roll the Dice on Your Next Night Out.' — Nunito 800, 48px, Velvet Plum (#2D2250), sentence case, centered, line-height 1.1, tight tracking (-0.02em). 16px top margin from eyebrow. This is the largest headline on a non-hero section — the Yellow background gives it room to breathe and makes it feel like a poster headline.

4. Subheadline: 'Tables fill up fast on weekends. Reserve yours now or take a peek inside the café first.' — DM Sans 400, 17px, Velvet Plum (#2D2250) at 80% opacity, line-height 1.6, max-width 480px, centered, 16px top margin from headline.

5. CTA button row (40px top margin, flex row, centered, 16px gap between buttons):
- Primary: 'Reserve a Table' — pill button, Rollout Blueberry (#3B6FE8) fill, Game Night White label, DM Sans 500 16px, 20px vertical / 36px horizontal padding.
- Secondary: 'Watch the Trailer' — pill button, Velvet Plum (#2D2250) fill, Game Night White label, same sizing. Using Velvet Plum (not an outline) on the Yellow background ensures both buttons read with equal visual weight and neither fights the background.

The Sun Token Yellow full-bleed panel is the section's defining move: it is the warmest, most cheerful surface on the page, reserved for the final ask. The Blueberry die icon hovering above the Velvet Plum headline on a Yellow field creates the brand's three primary colors in one tight composition — a visual summary of the Rollout identity.

RESPONSIVE: On mobile, the icon shrinks to 56px, headline to 36px, and CTA buttons stack vertically (full-width each, 12px gap).

## Games Page — Full Visual Design Direction

### Page Role & Goal
The Games page is a discovery-oriented overview that must make visitors feel the breadth and excitement of Rollout's library while removing any intimidation barrier. Every section should radiate warmth and playfulness — this is a candy store, not a catalogue.

---

### Signature Moment
**Section 2 (Genre Grid) — Oversized Floating Count Numbers as Background Typography**
Behind each genre card, the count number (e.g. "120+") is rendered in Fredoka One at approximately 96–120px, set in Playmat Mint at 8% opacity, sitting flush behind the card content like a watermark. This is NOT a subtle decorative touch — the numbers are large enough to peek out from behind the card title and icon, creating a layered typographic depth effect. This move is entirely native to the Friendly Consumer App aesthetic: it uses the brand's playful accent font at display scale, the mint accent color expressively (not just on buttons), and the rounded-card visual cue with added dimensionality. It communicates "abundance" without a single extra word. On mobile, the oversized number shifts to sit centered behind the card at reduced size (64px) so it remains visible within the single-column stack.

---

### Section Sequence & Rhythm

1. **Page Header (Section 1):** Dense, high-energy masthead with the illustration dominating the right side. Type-heavy left column. Coral accent panel behind the headline creates immediate color impact. Opens with maximum energy.

2. **Genre Grid (Section 2):** The signature moment section. Cloud Chalk background. Six rounded cards in a 3×2 grid, each with oversized mint watermark number. Dense but scannable. Medium padding.

3. **Staff Picks Feature Grid (Section 3):** Game Night White background. Horizontal card strip — four cards in a row at desktop, each with rich metadata chips. The section headline uses a pull-quote typographic treatment with a Sun Token Yellow underline accent drawn beneath "Can't Stop Recommending." Lighter, more editorial feel after the dense genre grid.

4. **Game Guides Story Block (Section 4):** Full-bleed Velvet Plum panel — the darkest surface on the page, creating a dramatic density break. Large reversed-out type. This is the emotional heart of the page. Asymmetric split: oversized illustrated character icon on the right at 60% panel height, body copy left-aligned on the left column. CTA in Playmat Mint.

5. **FAQ (Section 5):** Cloud Chalk background. Side-tabbed accordion layout — FAQ items stack vertically with Dice Coral left-border accents on the active/expanded state. Eyebrow and headline left-aligned. Right column holds the CTA card. Closes the page with a practical, helpful register that transitions into the Buy page.

---

### Color & Surface Logic
- Section 1 (Header): Game Night White background with a Dice Coral soft color block behind the headline text area (not full-bleed — a rectangular block sitting behind the H1 and subheadline, angled slightly, like a sticker backing). Illustration on right.
- Section 2 (Genre Grid): Cloud Chalk background. Cards on Game Night White with Playmat Mint oversized watermark numbers.
- Section 3 (Staff Picks): Game Night White background. Cards use Cloud Chalk fill with Rollout Blueberry metadata chip borders and Sun Token Yellow underline on headline.
- Section 4 (Game Guides): Full-bleed Velvet Plum panel. All type in Game Night White. CTA button in Playmat Mint with Velvet Plum text. Illustrated icon in Playmat Mint and Dice Coral tones.
- Section 5 (FAQ): Cloud Chalk background. FAQ items have Dice Coral left-border rule. CTA card on Game Night White with Rollout Blueberry button.

---

### Typographic Hierarchy
- H1 (Section 1): Nunito 800, 56–64px, Velvet Plum (on white) — "500+ Games and Counting." The "500+" numeral treated as a display moment in Fredoka One at the same size, Rollout Blueberry.
- H2 sections: Nunito 700, 36–42px, Velvet Plum on light surfaces, Game Night White on dark panels.
- Eyebrows: Fredoka One, 12px, wide letter-spacing (0.10em), color varies by section (Rollout Blueberry on light, Playmat Mint on dark).
- Body: DM Sans 400, 16–18px, Felt Gray on light surfaces, Game Night White at 85% opacity on dark panel.
- Card titles: Nunito 700, 20–22px.
- Metadata chips: DM Sans 500, 13px, Cloud Chalk background, Felt Gray text.
- FAQ titles: Nunito 700, 18–20px, Velvet Plum.
- FAQ answers: DM Sans 400, 16px, Felt Gray.

---

### Density / Whitespace Logic
- Section 1: Generous vertical padding (96px top, 80px bottom). Illustration fills the right half. Left column is compact but readable.
- Section 2: 64px vertical padding. Cards have 24px internal padding. The grid is intentionally dense — six cards feel like a full shelf.
- Section 3: 80px vertical padding. Four-card row with 24px gaps. Cards have 28px padding. Breathing room after the dense genre grid.
- Section 4: 96px vertical padding. Wide measure for body copy (max 60ch). Illustration is large and bleeds toward the right edge of the panel.
- Section 5: 80px vertical padding. FAQ items have 20px vertical gap between them. Right column CTA card has generous padding (32px).

---

### Responsive Behavior
- Desktop (≥1280px): All multi-column layouts as specified. Illustration in Section 1 takes 45% of width.
- Tablet (768–1279px): Section 2 genre grid collapses to 2×3. Section 3 staff picks to 2×2. Section 4 stacks vertically (illustration above body). Section 5 FAQ becomes full-width accordion, CTA card moves below.
- Mobile (<768px): All sections single-column. Section 1 illustration moves above the headline. Section 2 genre cards stack with oversized mint numbers at 64px. Section 3 cards stack. Section 4 illustration shrinks to 200px centered above copy. Section 5 full accordion stack.

---

### Cross-Page Rhythm
This page sits between the Home landing (high energy, broad) and the Trailer editorial (immersive, atmospheric). It must feel more organized and scannable than Home but warmer and more human than a pure catalogue. The Velvet Plum full-bleed panel in Section 4 is the deepest color moment on this page — echoing the footer's dark anchor — and creates the emotional peak before the practical FAQ close.

pages.page_level_design_instruction:
The Trailer page is Rollout's emotional centrepiece — a story-driven editorial journey that moves from cinematic atmosphere through intimate origin narrative, visual gallery richness, milestone timeline, and finally a warm conversion close. Unlike the more utility-driven Games or Buy pages, every section here is calibrated for *feeling* first, action second.

**Section rhythm and density logic:**
The page alternates between immersive, high-density editorial moments and airy, spacious story beats — never two dense sections back-to-back. Section 1 (page header) is full-bleed and visually dominant. Section 2 (story block) is intentionally sparse and intimate — wide measure prose, minimal decoration. Section 3 (gallery) is the densest section: a textured, pattern-backed mosaic of illustrated scene cards. Section 4 (timeline) is structured and vertical — a strong typographic spine. Section 5 (CTA close) returns to warmth and openness with a saturated Rollout Blueberry panel.

**Signature moment — the Gallery section's full-bleed illustrated pattern field with oversized floating scene titles:**
In Section 3, the board-game-element repeating pattern asset covers the entire section background as a full-bleed tinted field (Velvet Plum at ~90% opacity over Cloud Chalk, making the pattern subtly visible beneath). Each gallery card floats over this textured field with a Dice Coral top-border accent and a scene title rendered in Fredoka One at 28–32px — large enough to read as display type, not a card label. One card ("The Comeback") breaks the grid slightly, rotated ~2° and overlapping its neighbor, functioning as a physical sticker dropped on a game table. This is the page's signature moment: the combination of the patterned field, the oversized illustrated-card titles, and the one deliberately off-axis card creates a visual richness that feels unmistakably like a board game café's personality — playful, tactile, and alive — rather than a polished SaaS template.

**Color surface logic across the page:**
- Section 1: Game Night White background with a large Playmat Mint illustrative centrepiece; Velvet Plum headings.
- Section 2: Cloud Chalk background — the quietest surface on the page, letting the prose breathe; Velvet Plum body at slightly larger scale.
- Section 3: Velvet Plum full-bleed background with pattern overlay; card surfaces in Game Night White; Dice Coral card accents; Sun Token Yellow scene metadata labels.
- Section 4: Game Night White background; Sun Token Yellow timeline markers (large oversized numerals/year stamps); Velvet Plum headings; Rollout Blueberry CTA.
- Section 5: Rollout Blueberry full-bleed panel; Game Night White type; Playmat Mint secondary CTA button.

**Typographic hierarchy and expressive moves:**
- Nunito 700–800 drives all H1/H2 headings; sentence case throughout.
- Fredoka One eyebrow labels at 12–13px with 0.10em letter-spacing in the appropriate accent color per surface.
- DM Sans body at 17–18px, 1.65 line-height, max 68ch measure.
- In Section 4, the year stamps (2022, Early 2023, etc.) are rendered in Nunito 800 at 48–52px in Sun Token Yellow, acting as oversized numeral anchors beside each timeline entry — a typographic stunt that gives the timeline visual rhythm without photography.
- In Section 5, the headline "The Only Thing Better Than Watching Is Playing." is set at 48–54px centered, with "Watching" and "Playing" in Fredoka One (accent font) at the same scale but in Sun Token Yellow — creating a two-font weight contrast that makes those words feel like game pieces dropped into the sentence.

**Responsive behavior:**
- Section 1: Illustration scales down gracefully; headline drops from 60px to 38px at mobile; illustration moves above the text block.
- Section 2: Single column at all breakpoints; measure constrains naturally on mobile.
- Section 3: Gallery cards shift from a 3-column + 2-column masonry-style arrangement on desktop to a 2-column grid on tablet and single-column stacked cards on mobile; the rotated card resets to 0° on mobile to avoid clipping.
- Section 4: Timeline spine collapses from a two-column alternating left/right layout to a single left-aligned vertical list on mobile; year stamps remain large but reduce from 52px to 36px.
- Section 5: Two CTA buttons stack vertically on mobile; headline reduces to 34px.

**Shared design system coherence:**
All color tokens, font families, and spacing rhythms are drawn directly from the shared system. This page earns its distinctiveness through editorial composition — the pattern field, the oversized year stamps, the Fredoka One headline injection — rather than by introducing new colors or fonts. It feels like the most expressive page in the site while still being unmistakably Rollout.

## Community Page — Visual Design Plan

### Page Role & Emotional Target
This is the Community overview page. Its job is to make visitors feel that Rollout is a living, breathing social organism — not just a venue. Every visual decision should communicate warmth, belonging, and scale. The page must feel populated and alive, not like a polished marketing brochure.

### Signature Moment
The signature moment lives in **Section 3 (Stats)**. The four community statistics are rendered as enormous, oversized display numerals — "2,400+", "48", "320", "6" — set in Fredoka One at approximately 96–120px, each in a different palette accent (Rollout Blueberry, Playmat Mint, Dice Coral, Sun Token Yellow), arranged in a full-bleed Velvet Plum dark panel. The numerals bleed beyond their containing column boundaries, overlapping the panel edges and each other at a slight stagger, so they feel less like a data table and more like a bold typographic poster. Descriptor text sits beneath each numeral in Game Night White DM Sans. This move is grounded in the friendly-consumer-app aesthetic's "soft color blocks" and "large readable text" cues pushed to maximum amplitude — it turns a stats section into a page-defining moment of joyful visual density. The growth chart asset is embedded as a rounded card floating inside this dark panel, providing a data artifact that anchors the numbers without competing with the type.

### Section Sequence & Rhythm
1. **Page Header** — Generous centered hero with large illustration dominating the right two-thirds, headline left-anchored. Warm, open, inviting. Light surface.
2. **Item Grid (Events)** — Dense 3-column card grid on Cloud Chalk background. Cards are rounded, icon-tagged, with metadata pills. Busy but organized.
3. **Stats** — Full-bleed Velvet Plum dark panel. Oversized numeral type. The page's loudest, most saturated moment. Maximum visual energy. ← SIGNATURE MOMENT
4. **Article List** — Returns to light surface (Game Night White). Horizontal list layout, asymmetric, editorial feel. Quiet after the stat explosion. Sparse density.
5. **CTA Close** — Playmat Mint full-bleed soft color block. Centered composition. Friendly, rounded, warm. Two CTA buttons. Closes with invitation energy.

### Color & Surface Rhythm
- Section 1: Game Night White background
- Section 2: Cloud Chalk background (#EDF0F7) — gentle shift
- Section 3: Velvet Plum (#2D2250) full-bleed — dramatic dark break
- Section 4: Game Night White — breathing room returns
- Section 5: Playmat Mint (#3ECFB2) full-bleed — warm, energetic close

The page never repeats the same surface twice in a row. Dark/light/color contrast creates strong visual rhythm without monotony.

### Typographic Hierarchy
- H1 (Section 1): Nunito 700, 56–60px, Velvet Plum, sentence case, left-aligned
- H2 (Sections 2, 4, 5): Nunito 700, 36–42px
- Stat numerals (Section 3): Fredoka One, 96–120px, multi-color accents — this is the one moment Fredoka One escapes its "small accent" role and becomes a structural display element
- Eyebrow labels: Fredoka One, 12–13px, wide letter-spacing (0.10em), in brand accent colors
- Body: DM Sans 400, 16–18px, Felt Gray on light surfaces, Game Night White on dark
- Card labels/metadata: DM Sans 500, 13–14px, pill-styled

### Density Logic
The page alternates dense → sparse → explosive → editorial sparse → warm close. Section 2 is the most information-dense (6 cards). Section 3 is the most visually explosive. Section 4 is the most editorial and restrained. This creates a breathing rhythm that prevents fatigue across a long page.

### Responsive Behavior
- Section 1: Illustration stacks above headline on mobile; headline becomes centered
- Section 2: 3-col grid → 2-col → 1-col on mobile
- Section 3: 4 stats in a 2×2 grid on tablet, 1-col stacked on mobile; numerals scale down to 64–72px on mobile but remain dominant
- Section 4: Horizontal article rows become stacked cards on mobile
- Section 5: Two CTAs remain side-by-side on tablet, stack vertically on mobile

### Design System Fit
This page uses all eight palette colors across its five sections. Nunito, DM Sans, and Fredoka One all appear in their defined roles — except the deliberate signature escalation of Fredoka One in Section 3, which is a purposeful, grounded creative decision. Rounded cards, illustrated icons, and soft color blocks appear consistently. The page feels like a natural sibling to Home and Games while having its own distinct emotional register: communal, energetic, and celebratory.

pages.page_level_design_instruction:
The Buy page is Rollout's primary conversion engine — every design decision must reduce friction, build confidence, and make the three purchase actions (book a table, buy a game, grab an event ticket) feel effortless and exciting. The page is structured as five stacked vertical sections with deliberate rhythm variation: a bold masthead-style header, a transparent pricing grid, a warm product shop, a punchy event ticket grid, and a contact closer. No two consecutive sections share the same skeleton.

SIGNATURE MOMENT — "Three-Path Splash" in the Page Header (Section 1): The headline "Ready to Play? Let's Make It Official." is set in Fredoka One at an oversized display scale (~72–80px on desktop) spanning the full content width, breaking from the standard Nunito heading treatment to signal that this is the action page — the culmination of the site journey. The three illustrated icons (calendar, box, ticket) are not tucked in a corner; they are placed as large (80–96px each), equally spaced anchors directly beneath the headline, each sitting inside a soft Playmat Mint, Dice Coral, and Sun Token Yellow rounded pill/badge respectively — a full-width trio that acts as a visual navigation shortcut to the three conversion paths below. This move is calibrated to the Friendly Consumer App aesthetic: bold, bright, rounded, human, and immediately scannable. It belongs to this page because the Buy page must communicate "you can do three things here" in under two seconds.

SECTION RHYTHM AND SURFACE VARIATION:
— Section 1 (Page Header): Velvet Plum full-bleed background. Game Night White display headline. Three color-coded icon badges in a horizontal row. Sparse, confident, high-contrast. No body copy.
— Section 2 (Pricing): Game Night White surface. Four pricing cards in a 2×2 grid (not a standard 3-column row) with Cloud Chalk card backgrounds and Rollout Blueberry accent borders on the recommended tier. Dense but well-padded. One card (Extended Session) receives a "Most Popular" Playmat Mint badge. Asymmetric — the two private room cards are visually heavier (larger price callout, slightly taller card) than the two standard cards.
— Section 3 (Game Shop): Cloud Chalk alternating background. Six product cards in a 3×2 grid. A flat-lay mockup image spans the left third of the section header as a full-height bleed panel — product-display energy, not a polite illustration. Price tags rendered in Dice Coral pill labels. Staff-pick star ratings in Sun Token Yellow. Right two-thirds contains the headline stack and card grid.
— Section 4 (Event Tickets): Rollout Blueberry full-bleed background — a saturated color block that breaks the light-section rhythm and signals urgency. All text in Game Night White. Four event cards in a 2×2 grid with Cloud Chalk/semi-transparent card surfaces. Spot-count labels ("8 spots left") in Sun Token Yellow bold type. Free events labeled in Playmat Mint. This section is the page's energy spike.
— Section 5 (Contact Block): Game Night White surface with a Velvet Plum left-side accent panel (roughly 30% of width) containing the eyebrow and headline in large Nunito. The right 70% holds three contact method rows (email, phone, gift vouchers) as horizontal list items with illustrated icons, plus the CTA. Asymmetric split that mirrors the masthead energy of Section 1 as a closing bookend.

COLOR LOGIC: Velvet Plum anchors the open and close (Sections 1 and 5). Rollout Blueberry dominates Section 4 as a full-bleed urgency panel and appears on all primary CTAs. Playmat Mint appears on the "Most Popular" badge and free-event labels. Dice Coral carries price tags and sale energy in Section 3. Sun Token Yellow marks ratings and scarcity signals. Cloud Chalk provides card surface texture in Sections 2 and 4. Game Night White is the primary page canvas.

TYPOGRAPHY: Fredoka One at 72–80px for the Section 1 display headline (signature moment). Nunito 700 at 42px for Section 2–4 section headlines. Nunito 700 at 36px for Section 5 headline (inside dark panel). DM Sans 400/500 at 16–18px for all body and card descriptions. Fredoka One at 11–14px with wide letter-spacing for all eyebrow labels. Price callouts in Nunito 800 at 28–32px in Velvet Plum or Game Night White depending on surface.

DENSITY AND WHITESPACE: Section 1 is sparse — generous vertical padding (80–100px top/bottom), large type, three icons, nothing else. Section 2 is medium-dense — cards with comfortable internal padding (24px), 24px gaps. Section 3 is the densest section — 6 product cards plus a bleed image. Section 4 is medium-dense on a saturated background — the color does the visual work so card density can breathe. Section 5 is sparse and confident — the asymmetric split and three list items with generous line height.

RESPONSIVE BEHAVIOR: On mobile, Section 1 headline drops to ~48px Fredoka One; three icon badges stack vertically or collapse to a 3-column icon row at reduced size. Section 2 pricing cards become a single-column scroll. Section 3 product grid becomes 2 columns; the flat-lay mockup moves above the headline stack as a full-width image. Section 4 event cards stack to single column. Section 5 asymmetric split collapses to stacked: dark panel above, contact list below.

This page fits the shared design system by using all eight palette colors purposefully, maintaining Nunito/DM Sans/Fredoka One hierarchy, and applying rounded cards and friendly CTAs throughout — while standing apart from other pages through its Velvet Plum opener, Blueberry urgency panel, and Fredoka One display headline signature moment.
